title: matplotlib: two histograms
source:
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

weights = [3.1, 3.4, 2.9, 3.8, 3.3, 3.6, 4.0, 3.2, 3.5, 2.7, 3.9, 3.4, 3.0, 3.7, 3.3, 3.6]

plt.hist(weights, bins=4, edgecolor="black")
plt.title("Melon weights, 4 bins")
plt.xlabel("Weight (kg)")
plt.show()

plt.hist(weights, bins=8, edgecolor="black", color="tab:purple")
plt.title("Melon weights, 8 bins")
plt.xlabel("Weight (kg)")
plt.ylabel("Melons")
plt.show()

steps.narration: weights now refers to a new list.
Drew a histogram of the values in weights on the current axes, sorted into 4 bins.
Set the title of the current axes to "Melon weights, 4 bins".
Set the x-axis label of the current axes to "Weight (kg)".
Figure 1 is in the output: a histogram titled Melon weights, 4 bins, with the x axis labelled Weight (kg).
Drew a histogram of the values in weights on the current axes, sorted into 8 bins.
Set the title of the current axes to "Melon weights, 8 bins".
Set the x-axis label of the current axes to "Weight (kg)".
Set the y-axis label of the current axes to "Melons".
Figure 2 is in the output: a histogram titled Melon weights, 8 bins, with the x axis labelled Weight (kg) and the y axis Melons.
